title: Where each log lives on Windows and on Linux

videos.script: In the middle of an incident, nobody has time to wonder where a log is kept. {{rush}} You open the right file, or the right channel, and you read the right line. This lesson is the map. {{map}} On Linux, most of it is text, under one folder. You will see who writes those files, how the lines are sorted, and who is allowed to read them. {{linux}} Then the journal, which keeps the same messages in another shape. On Windows, logs are channels, and an event is known by its number. {{windows}} A dozen of those numbers cover most of what an analyst asks about. You will learn them, and their Linux counterparts. And the last section is about time. A line with the wrong time zone puts an event in the wrong hour of the wrong night. {{time}}
